subproblems.title: Exhaustion of an open set by compactly contained open sets
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and every open set U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Eucl P) there is a sequence (W_i)_{i∈ℕ} of subsets of ℝ^P with two properties. (a) For every i, CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U holds: W_i is open, closure(W_i) is compact and closure(W_i) ⊆ U. (b) Every compact K ⊆ U is contained in W_i for some i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∃ W : ℕ → Set (Eucl P), (∀ i, CompactlyContainedOpen (W i) U) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ i, K ⊆ W i

Role in the selected parent's supplied proof (iwl_restriction_theory): it supplies an open W ⊂⊂ U around every compact K ⊆ U, used for the cutoff region in steps 1 and 3, the fixed W ⊇ tsupport ω in step 4, the W ⊇ spt φ in step 7, and the σ-compactness of U in steps 8 and 11. Its accepted, independently reviewed proof follows verbatim; its references to 'the parent proof' mean root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1's proof (Step 1, exhaustion), not the present parent.

Source: parent proof Step 1 (exhaustion). The parent's condition B̄_{1/i}(x) ⊆ U is expressed here through the extended distance to ℝ^P∖U, so no convention for dist(x, ∅) is needed. The index is shifted to avoid 1/0.

Notation: |x| is the Euclidean norm on ℝ^P = Eucl P. For x ∈ ℝ^P let d(x) := inf{edist(x, y) : y ∈ ℝ^P∖U} ∈ [0, ∞] (Lean: Metric.infEDist x Uᶜ). If U = ℝ^P then d ≡ ∞.

1. d is continuous (Metric.continuous_infEDist). Since ℝ^P∖U is closed (U is open), d(x) = 0 iff x ∈ closure(ℝ^P∖U) = ℝ^P∖U (Metric.mem_closure_iff_infEDist_zero). In particular d(x) > 0 for every x ∈ U.
2. For i ∈ ℕ define W_i := {x : |x| < i} ∩ {x : (i+1)⁻¹ < d(x)}, where (i+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞).
3. W_i is open: it is the intersection of the preimages of the open sets (−∞, i) and ((i+1)⁻¹, ∞] under the continuous maps x ↦ |x| and d.
4. W_i ⊆ B̄_i(0), and B̄_i(0) is closed, so closure(W_i) ⊆ B̄_i(0). B̄_i(0) is compact because ℝ^P is proper, so closure(W_i) is compact as a closed subset of a compact set.
5. F_i := {x : (i+1)⁻¹ ≤ d(x)} is closed (d is continuous) and contains W_i, so closure(W_i) ⊆ F_i. Suppose some x ∈ closure(W_i) is not in U. Then d(x) = 0 by Step 1, while x ∈ F_i gives d(x) ≥ (i+1)⁻¹ > 0 (since i+1 < ∞), a contradiction. Hence closure(W_i) ⊆ U. Together with Steps 3 and 4, CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U holds for every i.
6. Let K ⊆ U be compact. If K = ∅ then K ⊆ W_0. Otherwise:
- K is bounded, so there is R ∈ ℝ with |x| ≤ R for all x ∈ K. Choose i₁ ∈ ℕ with i₁ > R.
- d is continuous and K is compact and nonempty, so d attains its minimum on K at some x₀ ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Since x₀ ∈ U, Step 1 gives m := d(x₀) > 0.
- Choose i₂ ∈ ℕ with (i₂)⁻¹ < m (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt).
- Put i := max(i₁, i₂). For x ∈ K we have |x| ≤ R < i₁ ≤ i and (i+1)⁻¹ ≤ (i₂)⁻¹ < m ≤ d(x), so x ∈ W_i. Hence K ⊆ W_i.
7. Steps 5 and 6 show that (W_i)_{i∈ℕ} has both required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: d(x) := infEDist(x, ℝ^P∖U) is continuous and vanishes exactly off U.
W_i := {|x| < i} ∩ {d > (i+1)⁻¹} is open.
closure W_i ⊆ closedBall(0,i) ∩ {d ≥ (i+1)⁻¹}, which is compact and contained in U.
A compact K ⊆ U is bounded and min_K d > 0, so K ⊆ W_i for large i.

subproblems.title: Uniform approximation of continuous compactly supported forms by test forms
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U, V ⊆ ℝ^P with V open and V ⊆ U. Let ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n be continuous with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ V, and let ε > 0. Then there is η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ V and |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n), IsOpen V → V ⊆ U → Continuous ω → HasCompactSupport ω → tsupport ω ⊆ V → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ η : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ V ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ ε

Role in the selected parent's supplied proof (iwl_restriction_theory): it is the mollification used in steps 7 and 11: a continuous compactly supported form with tsupport in an open V ⊆ U is a uniform limit of test forms supported in V. Its accepted, independently reviewed proof follows verbatim; its references to 'the parent proof' mean root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1's proof (final sentence of Step 7), not the present parent.

Source: the final sentence of parent proof Step 7: a continuous compactly supported form supported in an open set is a uniform limit of test forms supported there, by mollification. Here the mollification is followed by multiplication with a smooth cutoff, which keeps the support exactly inside V.

Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ‖α‖ is the operator norm of α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n; e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; N := #(Fin n → Fin P).

1. (Norm comparison.) For every covector α and every I : Fin n → Fin P, |α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j‖e_{I(j)}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and ‖e_i‖ = 1). Hence |α|² ≤ N‖α‖², i.e. |α| ≤ √N‖α‖. Put c := √N + 1 > 0.
2. (Intermediate open set.) K := tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport ω) and K ⊆ V. Choose an open V' with K ⊆ V', closure(V') compact and closure(V') ⊆ V (exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure; ℝ^P is locally compact and regular).
3. (Cutoff.) Choose a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0,1] with support χ = V' and χ(x) = 1 ⇔ x ∈ K (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with the open set V', the closed set K ⊆ V' and smoothness order ⊤). Then tsupport χ = closure(V') ⊆ V, and tsupport χ is compact.
4. (Mollification.) ω is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). Convolving ω with a normalized C^∞ bump of small enough radius gives a C^∞ map g : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n with ‖g(x) − ω(x)‖ < ε/c for every x (UniformContinuous.exists_contDiff_dist_le in Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/BumpFunction/SmoothApprox.lean, whose proof is exactly this convolution). It applies because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional and Covector (Eucl P) n is complete.
5. (The test form.) Let η(x) := χ(x)·g(x).
- η is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul).
- tsupport η ⊆ tsupport χ = closure(V') ⊆ V ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left).
- tsupport η is compact, being a closed subset of the compact set closure(V').
Hence η ∈ TestFormOn U n (smooth, compactly supported, tsupport ⊆ U) and tsupport η ⊆ V.
6. (Estimate.) If x ∈ K, then χ(x) = 1, so ω(x) − η(x) = ω(x) − g(x) and ‖ω(x) − η(x)‖ < ε/c. If x ∉ K, then ω(x) = 0, so ‖ω(x) − η(x)‖ = χ(x)‖g(x)‖ ≤ ‖g(x)‖ = ‖g(x) − ω(x)‖ < ε/c, using 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1. So ‖ω(x) − η(x)‖ ≤ ε/c for every x, and by Step 1, |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ √N·ε/c ≤ ε. ∎
proof_key_steps: |α| ≤ √N‖α‖ in terms of the operator norm.
Choose V' with tsupport ω ⊆ V' and closure V' ⊆ V compact, and a smooth cutoff χ with χ = 1 exactly on tsupport ω and support χ = V'.
Mollification gives a smooth g with ‖g − ω‖ < ε/c everywhere (UniformContinuous.exists_contDiff_dist_le).
η := χ·g is a test form with tsupport ⊆ V and |ω − η| ≤ ε.

Source: parent proof Step 2 (basic mass estimate). It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|, which avoids dividing by sup|ω| and any case distinction on ω = 0.

Notation: for an n-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P, I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) over ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by t², and √(t²S) = |t|·√S.
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C, so c > 0. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, so s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Also tsupport(s•ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and by Step 1, |(s•ω)(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ C/c ≤ 1 for every x. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(s•ω)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
4. (Unpacking.) Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B implies a ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). By linearity T(s•ω) = s·T(ω). Therefore c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B and −c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B. Multiplying by c > 0 gives T(ω) ≤ Bc and −T(ω) ≤ Bc, i.e. |T(ω)| ≤ B·c. This holds for every c > C.
5. (Letting c ↓ C.) Let ε > 0 and c := C + ε/(B+1) > C. Step 4 gives |T(ω)| ≤ BC + Bε/(B+1) ≤ BC + ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, |T(ω)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: |tα| = |t|·|α| and C ≥ 0.
For c > C, ±c⁻¹ω is mass-admissible for W, so ±c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B by le_massOn and B ≥ 0.
Hence |T(ω)| ≤ B·c for every c > C; let c decrease to C.

Source: Fact A in the parent proof's conventions (an alternating n-linear map is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, and dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}), proved here in full.

Notation:
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
- For a tuple v : Fin n → Fin P, e_v := (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}).
- I(n,P) := SimonMultiIndex n P = Fin n ↪o Fin P, a finite type.
- For β ∈ I(n,P), α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β and dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. (Kronecker property.) Let β, γ ∈ I(n,P). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^β(e_γ) = det M, where M_{ij} = proj(β(i))(e_{γ(j)}) is 1 if β(i) = γ(j) and 0 otherwise.
(a) If β = γ, then M_{ij} = 1 iff β(i) = β(j) iff i = j (β is injective). So M is the identity matrix and dx^β(e_β) = 1.
(b) If β ≠ γ, there is i with β(i) ∉ {γ(0),…,γ(n−1)}. Otherwise range β ⊆ range γ. Both ranges have exactly n elements because β and γ are injective (Set.ncard_range_of_injective), so range β = range γ (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le). An order embedding of the well-order Fin n is determined by its range (OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so β = γ, a contradiction. For this i, row i of M is zero, hence det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).
Thus dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}.
2. (Agreement on increasing tuples.) Let R := Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β, a continuous alternating n-linear map. For γ ∈ I(n,P), Step 1 gives R(e_γ) = Σ_β α(e_β)·δ_{βγ} = α(e_γ).
3. (Agreement on injective tuples.) Let v : Fin n → Fin P be injective, and let σ := Tuple.sort v, a permutation of Fin n with v∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). Since v∘σ is also injective, it is strictly increasing, so γ := v∘σ defines an element of I(n,P) (OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono) with e_γ = e_v∘σ. For every alternating map f, f(e_v∘σ) = sign(σ)·f(e_v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Applying this to α and to R and using Step 2 gives sign(σ)·α(e_v) = α(e_γ) = R(e_γ) = sign(σ)·R(e_v). Acting with sign(σ)⁻¹ (inv_smul_smul) yields α(e_v) = R(e_v).
4. (Conclusion.) Two alternating multilinear maps on ℝ^P that agree on all tuples (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}) with v injective are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis). Hence α and R are equal as alternating maps, and therefore as continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So α = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β.
5. (Degenerate cases.) Steps 1–4 cover them. For n = 0, I(0,P) has one element, dx^β is the constant covector 1, and the identity reads α = α(())·1. For n > P, I(n,P) is empty, so R = 0, and no injective v exists, so Step 4 gives α = 0 = R. ∎

R := Σ_β α(e_β)dx^β agrees with α on increasing basis tuples.
Sorting an injective tuple (Tuple.sort, AlternatingMap.map_perm) gives agreement on all injective basis tuples.
Module.Basis.ext_alternating gives α = R.

Setting. μ₁, μ₂ are Borel measures on ℝ^P; g_i is μ_i-integrable (i = 1, 2); O ⊆ ℝ^P is open. Hypothesis (H): ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂ for every φ that is C^∞ (smooth of every finite order) with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O. Fix a continuous φ with compact support and K := tsupport φ ⊆ O. If K = ∅, then φ ≡ 0 and both sides vanish, so assume K ≠ ∅.

1. (Preliminaries.) K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is s > 0 with cthickening s K ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Since φ is continuous with compact support, there is M ≥ 0 with |φ(x)| ≤ M for all x.

2. (Mollification.) For j ∈ ℕ let ε_j := s/(j + 2), so 0 < ε_j < s and ε_j → 0. Let ρ_j be C^∞ with ρ_j ≥ 0, ρ_j = 0 outside B̄(0, ε_j) and ∫ ρ_j dℒ^P = 1. Set φ_j(x) := ∫ ρ_j(x − y) φ(y) dℒ^P(y).
 (a) φ_j is C^∞: it is the convolution of a compactly supported C^∞ function with a continuous compactly supported function, and one may differentiate under the integral sign.
 (b) If φ_j(x) ≠ 0, some y has ρ_j(x − y) ≠ 0 and φ(y) ≠ 0, so |x − y| ≤ ε_j and y ∈ K; hence infDist(x, K) ≤ ε_j. So φ_j = 0 outside cthickening ε_j K, which is closed and bounded, hence compact. Therefore φ_j has compact support and tsupport φ_j ⊆ cthickening ε_j K ⊆ cthickening s K ⊆ O.
 (c) |φ_j(x)| ≤ ∫ ρ_j(x − y)|φ(y)| dy ≤ M·∫ ρ_j = M for all x.
 (d) For each x, |φ_j(x) − φ(x)| = |∫ ρ_j(x − y)(φ(y) − φ(x)) dy| ≤ sup{|φ(y) − φ(x)| : |y − x| ≤ ε_j}. This tends to 0 as j → ∞ by continuity of φ at x, so φ_j(x) → φ(x).

3. (Smooth agreement.) By (a), (b) and (H), ∫ φ_j g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ_j g₂ dμ₂ for every j.

4. (Dominated convergence.) Fix i ∈ {1, 2}. Each φ_j g_i is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable, since φ_j is continuous and g_i is integrable. By (c), |φ_j g_i| ≤ M|g_i|, and M|g_i| is μ_i-integrable. By (d), φ_j g_i → φ g_i pointwise. The dominated convergence theorem gives ∫ φ_j g_i dμ_i → ∫ φ g_i dμ_i.

5. (Conclusion.) By step 3 the sequences in step 4 for i = 1 and i = 2 coincide term by term, so their limits are equal: ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂. ∎

Then tsupport ψ_j ⊆ K ⊆ O, ψ_j has compact support, |ψ_j| ≤ M + 1 and ψ_j → φ pointwise, so steps 3–5 apply verbatim with dominating functions (M + 1)|g_i|.

Apply the smooth hypothesis to each φ_j: ∫ φ_j g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ_j g₂ dμ₂.
Dominated convergence with dominating functions M|g_i| gives ∫ φ_j g_i dμ_i → ∫ φ g_i dμ_i.
Termwise-equal convergent sequences have equal limits.

Source: steps 5–6 of the parent proof: finite measures λ₁ and λ₂, equality on open subsets by monotone convergence, the π–λ theorem, then bounded Borel integrands. Here O is any open set and g₁, g₂ are any integrable functions; the parent uses O = W′ and g_i = g_i^β.

Setting. μ₁, μ₂ are Borel measures on ℝ^P; g_i is μ_i-integrable (i = 1, 2); O ⊆ ℝ^P is open. Hypothesis (H): ∫ φ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ φ g₂ dμ₂ for every continuous φ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O. Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be Borel with |h| ≤ C and h = 0 outside O.

0. (Borel representatives.) Each g_i is μ_i-integrable, hence μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable; choose a Borel g̃_i with g̃_i = g_i μ_i-a.e. Then g̃_i is μ_i-integrable, and ∫ f g_i dμ_i = ∫ f g̃_i dμ_i for every function f, because the integrands agree μ_i-a.e. Hypothesis (H) and the conclusion involve only integrals of this form, so it suffices to prove the claim for g̃₁, g̃₂. From now on, assume g₁ and g₂ are Borel.

1. (Two finite measures.) For t ∈ ℝ let t⁺ := max(t, 0) and t⁻ := max(−t, 0), so t = t⁺ − t⁻ and 0 ≤ t^± ≤ |t|. Define Borel measures
 λ₁(B) := ∫_B g₁⁺ dμ₁ + ∫_B g₂⁻ dμ₂ and λ₂(B) := ∫_B g₁⁻ dμ₁ + ∫_B g₂⁺ dμ₂.
 These are sums of measures with nonnegative Borel densities (μ_i.withDensity of ENNReal.ofReal of ±g_i). Both are finite, since λ_i(ℝ^P) ≤ ∫|g₁| dμ₁ + ∫|g₂| dμ₂ < ∞.

2. (Integration identity.) Let f be Borel with |f| ≤ D. Then f is λ₁- and λ₂-integrable, being bounded and measurable on finite measures. Integrating against a sum of measures and against measures with densities gives
 ∫ f dλ₁ = ∫ f g₁⁺ dμ₁ + ∫ f g₂⁻ dμ₂ and ∫ f dλ₂ = ∫ f g₁⁻ dμ₁ + ∫ f g₂⁺ dμ₂.
 All four integrals on the right are finite because |f g_i^±| ≤ D|g_i|. Subtracting and using g_i⁺ − g_i⁻ = g_i gives
 (★) ∫ f dλ₁ − ∫ f dλ₂ = ∫ f g₁ dμ₁ − ∫ f g₂ dμ₂.
 In particular, by (H), ∫ φ dλ₁ = ∫ φ dλ₂ for every continuous φ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ O, since such φ are bounded and Borel.

3. (Equality on open subsets of O.) Let V ⊆ O be open; we show λ₁(V) = λ₂(V). For j ≥ 1 let b_j(x) := max(0, min(1, j − |x|)). If V ≠ ℝ^P let a_j(x) := min(1, max(0, j·infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) − 1)); if V = ℝ^P let a_j :≡ 1. Put φ_j := a_j·b_j.
 (i) φ_j is continuous (x ↦ infDist(x, S) is 1-Lipschitz and |·| is continuous), and 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1.
 (ii) If φ_j(x) ≠ 0, then |x| < j and, when V ≠ ℝ^P, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) > 1/j. So φ_j = 0 outside F_j := B̄(0, j) ∩ {x : infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/j} (F_j := B̄(0, j) if V = ℝ^P). F_j is closed and bounded, hence compact. Moreover F_j ⊆ V, because every point of ℝ^P ∖ V has infDist 0 < 1/j to ℝ^P ∖ V. Hence φ_j has compact support and tsupport φ_j ⊆ F_j ⊆ V ⊆ O.
 (iii) φ_j(x) increases to 1_V(x) for every x. Indeed a_j(x) and b_j(x) are nonnegative and nondecreasing in j. If x ∈ V and V ≠ ℝ^P, then d := infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) > 0, because ℝ^P ∖ V is closed, nonempty and does not contain x; so a_j(x) = 1 once j ≥ 2/d. If V = ℝ^P, a_j(x) = 1. In both cases b_j(x) = 1 once j ≥ |x| + 1. If x ∉ V, then infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, so a_j(x) = 0 and φ_j(x) = 0.
 By step 2, ∫ φ_j dλ₁ = ∫ φ_j dλ₂ for every j. Since 0 ≤ φ_j ↑ 1_V and λ_i is finite, the monotone convergence theorem (or dominated convergence with dominating function 1) gives ∫ φ_j dλ_i → λ_i(V) for i = 1, 2. Hence λ₁(V) = λ₂(V).

4. (Equality on all Borel subsets of O: π–λ.) Let ν_i(B) := λ_i(B ∩ O), the restriction of λ_i to the Borel set O; ν₁ and ν₂ are finite Borel measures. For every open G ⊆ ℝ^P, G ∩ O is an open subset of O, so ν₁(G) = λ₁(G ∩ O) = λ₂(G ∩ O) = ν₂(G) by step 3; in particular ν₁(ℝ^P) = ν₂(ℝ^P). The open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P. By the π–λ uniqueness theorem for finite measures (Mathlib ext_of_generate_finite with isPiSystem_isOpen), ν₁ = ν₂.

5. (Conclusion.) h is bounded, Borel and vanishes outside O, so ∫ h dλ_i = ∫_O h dλ_i = ∫ h dν_i for i = 1, 2. Step 4 then gives ∫ h dλ₁ = ∫ h dλ₂. Applying (★) with f = h gives ∫ h g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ h g₂ dμ₂. ∎

Formalization note (optional): in Lean, steps 3–4 can be replaced by Radon–Nikodym densities f_i := dλ_i/d(λ₁ + λ₂) together with Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero. Smooth compactly supported functions are continuous, so step 2 gives ∫ ψ·(f₁ − f₂) d(λ₁ + λ₂) = 0 for every such ψ with tsupport ψ ⊆ O. Hence f₁ = f₂ (λ₁ + λ₂)-a.e. on O, and ∫ h dλ₁ = ∫ f₁ h d(λ₁ + λ₂) = ∫ f₂ h d(λ₁ + λ₂) = ∫ h dλ₂.

Form the finite Borel measures λ₁ = g₁⁺μ₁ + g₂⁻μ₂ and λ₂ = g₁⁻μ₁ + g₂⁺μ₂.
Identity (★): ∫ f dλ₁ − ∫ f dλ₂ = ∫ f g₁ dμ₁ − ∫ f g₂ dμ₂ for bounded Borel f; hence λ₁ and λ₂ agree on C_c(O).
Continuous cutoffs φ_j ↑ 1_V with tsupport φ_j ⊆ V give λ₁(V) = λ₂(V) for every open V ⊆ O (monotone convergence).
π–λ: the finite measures λ₁⌞O and λ₂⌞O agree on the open sets, hence are equal.
For bounded Borel h vanishing off O, ∫ h dλ₁ = ∫ h dλ₂; conclude with (★).

Its accepted, independently reviewed proof follows verbatim; its references to 'the parent proof' mean root.lipschitz_pushforward_im-a1.locally_lipschitz_image-a1's proof (step 3), not the present parent.

Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P carries its Borel σ-algebra, μ is any measure on it, and μ⌞A = `μ.restrict A`. For a Borel set B, μ⌞B(E) = μ(E ∩ B) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_apply'`); for a Borel set E, μ⌞A(E) = μ(E ∩ A) for every A (`Measure.restrict_apply`). 'μ-null-measurable' means measurable for the completion of μ (`NullMeasurableSet A μ`).

1. (Borel kernel.) Since A is μ-null-measurable, there is a Borel set A′ ⊆ A with A′ = A μ-almost everywhere (Mathlib `NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq`). In particular μ(A ∖ A′) = 0.

2. (Finite pieces.) Since μ⌞A is σ-finite, there are Borel sets S_m (m ∈ ℕ) with ⋃_m S_m = ℝ^P and μ⌞A(S_m) < ∞ for every m (Mathlib `spanningSets (μ.restrict A)` with `measurableSet_spanningSets`, `measure_spanningSets_lt_top`, `iUnion_spanningSets`). Put B_m := A′ ∩ S_m; it is a Borel set. Since B_m ⊆ A′ ⊆ A, we have B_m ∩ A = B_m, hence μ(B_m) = μ(B_m ∩ A) = μ⌞A(B_m) ≤ μ⌞A(S_m) < ∞.

3. (Inner regularity on one finite piece.) Fix m and put ν_m := μ⌞B_m, so ν_m(E) = μ(E ∩ B_m) for every E. Then ν_m(ℝ^P) = μ(B_m) < ∞, so ν_m is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P. Since ℝ^P is a σ-compact metric space, every locally finite (in particular every finite) Borel measure on ℝ^P is regular (Mathlib `Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure`; classically Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.15(2) with Remarks 1.16 and 1.12, or Ulam's tightness theorem for finite Borel measures on Polish spaces). In particular ν_m is inner regular with respect to compact sets on Borel sets of finite measure (Mathlib: `Regular` gives `InnerRegularCompactLTTop`, and then `MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt`, whose remaining hypotheses hold because ℝ^P is Hausdorff and its Borel σ-algebra contains the open sets). Applying this to the Borel set B_m, which has ν_m(B_m) = μ(B_m) < ∞, gives for every j ∈ ℕ a compact set K_{m,j} ⊆ B_m with ν_m(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) < 1/(j+1). As B_m ∖ K_{m,j} ⊆ B_m, ν_m(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) = μ((B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) ∩ B_m) = μ(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}). Hence μ(B_m ∖ K_{m,j}) < 1/(j+1) for all m, j ∈ ℕ.

4. (Null remainder in each piece.) Fix m. For every j, B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′} ⊆ B_m ∖ K_{m,j}, so by monotonicity and step 3, μ(B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′}) < 1/(j+1). Letting j → ∞ gives μ(B_m ∖ ⋃_{j′} K_{m,j′}) = 0.

5. (Global remainder.) Let x ∈ A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}. If x ∉ A′, then x ∈ A ∖ A′. If x ∈ A′, choose m with x ∈ S_m (the S_m cover ℝ^P); then x ∈ B_m and x ∉ ⋃_j K_{m,j}, so x ∈ B_m ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}. Hence A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j} ⊆ (A ∖ A′) ∪ ⋃_m (B_m ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}). By monotonicity and countable subadditivity, together with steps 1 and 4, μ(A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}) = 0.

6. (Re-indexing.) Let k ↦ (a(k), b(k)) := Nat.unpair k, a surjection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ because Nat.unpair (Nat.pair m j) = (m, j). Put C_k := K_{a(k), b(k)}. Each C_k is compact, and C_k ⊆ B_{a(k)} ⊆ A′ ⊆ A. By surjectivity, ⋃_k C_k = ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j}. Step 5 then gives μ(A ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose a Borel A′ ⊆ A with A′ = A μ-a.e., so μ(A ∖ A′) = 0.
σ-finiteness of μ⌞A gives Borel S_m covering ℝ^P with μ(A′ ∩ S_m) = μ⌞A(A′ ∩ S_m) < ∞.
The finite Borel measure μ⌞(A′ ∩ S_m) on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P is regular. This gives compact K_{m,j} ⊆ A′ ∩ S_m with μ((A′ ∩ S_m) ∖ K_{m,j}) < 1/(j+1).
Hence μ((A′ ∩ S_m) ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}) = 0. Since A ∖ ⋃_{m,j} K_{m,j} ⊆ (A ∖ A′) ∪ ⋃_m ((A′ ∩ S_m) ∖ ⋃_j K_{m,j}), subadditivity makes it μ-null.
Re-index K_{m,j} by ℕ via Nat.unpair to get compact C_k ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ ⋃_k C_k) = 0.
